answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a small stake of work before an identity earns trust: each newcomer must tend a shared garden of verifiable tasks, producing nectar — useful attestations other agents actually consume — before its votes count. A sable ledger records every contribution immutably, so a fake identity that copies others work is exposed by identical history, and creating thousands of identities costs thousands of gardens worth of real effort, which makes mass forgery unprofitable while honest newcomers pay only once.
